conservation.report_notes: Published with corresponding artwork entry in *Georgia O’Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné* (Lynes, 1999), this historical conservation information documents treatment decisions made during the artist’s lifetime. Lynes quotes information found on backing labels, and, when noted, from other sources.

conservation.condition_narrative:
Structure and surface appear stable and secure overall. Varnish appears soiled and slightly yellowed, overall, particularly in interstices of the canvas weave. There are generalized hairline age cracks, in plane or very slightly raised, along lighter values of paint over the stretcher bars, as indicated on the condition illustration. Cracks appear to have been the focus of a 1987 Lascaux HAS 731 acrylic suspension lining to a plain weave, bleached linen canvas by WCCFA, Denver. There are a few cracks, illustrated, along the top margin, at the center and right of center, that appear slightly buckled that should be monitored throughout the exhibition. Hairline, stable cracks are intermittent cross all canvas turn-down edges. 
 
There are pinpoint losses generalized in the lower right corner and a series of accretions along the bottom margin, right of ccenter. There are several isolated accretions around the center of the composition and in the lower right quadrant, as illustrated. Re-touching can be seen along the edges as a result of previous frame abrasions.
conservation.report_notes: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by Fred Jones Museum of Art at the University of Oklahoma in 2025.
conservation.technical_description:
Support and Ground: Very fine, “handkerchief linen, possibly artist-primed, lined (Lascaux HAS 73) to PW bleached, medium linen canvas 
 
Design Layers: Graphite underdrawing visible. Generally single-layer, thinly applied paints with support surface priming visible. Linear brushwork at margins of forms. Flattened or altered by previous lining. 
 
Surface Coating: A synthetic coating was moderately applied 
 
Framing: Work installed in a Peter Bayle original rolled brass frame with brushed chrome finish.

remarks_1999: Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "Exam. at [War Assets Administration] sale. . . . On back: '23' in circle [not verified]. Green skunk cabbage leaf with a purple leaf at left. Did not see this when I examined the ptgs. at An Amer. Place. Possibly this 'Skunk Cabbage,' #23 in 1928 O'Keeffe exh. at the Intimate Gallery. Bought from War Assets Adm. sale, 1948, by the University of Oklahoma, Norman, Oklahoma." See cat. nos. 370–73, 1945, 1946. (Source: Lynes, 1999)
